items.text:
Technology is never a neutral tool for achieving human ends. Technological innovations reshape people as they use these innovations to control their environment. Artificial intelligence, for example, is altering humanity.
While the term AI conjures up anxieties about killer robots or catastrophic levels of unemployment, there are other, deeper implications. As AI increasingly shapes the human experience, how does this change what it means to be human?Central to the problem is a person's capacity to make choices, particularly judgments that have moral implications.
Aristotle argued that the capacity for making practical judgments depends on regularly making them — on habit and practice. We see the emergence of machines as substitute judges in a variety of everyday contexts as a potential threat to people learning how to effectively exercise judgment themselves.

q.stem: What do we learn about the deeper implications of AI?
options: It is causing catastrophic levels of unemployment.
It is doing physical harm to human operators.
It is altering moral judgments.
It is reshaping humanity.
q.explain: 正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「While the term AI conjures up anxieties about killer robots or catastrophic levels of unemployment, there are other, deeper implications.」

We see the emergence of machines as substitute judges in a variety of everyday contexts as a potential threat to people learning how to effectively exercise judgment themselves.
In the workplace, managers routinely make decisions about who to hire or fire and which loan to approve, to name a few. These are areas where _algorithmic_ (算法的) prescription is replacing human judgment, and so people who might have had the chance to develop practical judgment in these areas no longer will.
Recommendation engines, which are increasingly prevalent intermediaries in people's consumption of culture, may serve to constrain choice and minimize luck. By presenting consumers with algorithmically selected choices of what to watch, read, stream and visit next, companies are replacing human taste with machine taste. In one sense, this is helpful. After all, machines can survey a wider range of choices than any individual is likely to have the time or energy to do on their own.

q.stem: What is the consequence of algorithmic prescription replacing human judgment?
options: People lose the chance to cultivate the ability to make practical judgments.
People are prevented from participating in making major decisions in the workplace.
Managers no longer have the chance to decide which loan to approve.
Managers do not need to take the trouble to determine who to hire or fire.

Recommendation engines, which are increasingly prevalent intermediaries in people's consumption of culture, may serve to constrain choice and minimize luck. By presenting consumers with algorithmically selected choices of what to watch, read, stream and visit next, companies are replacing human taste with machine taste. In one sense, this is helpful. After all, machines can survey a wider range of choices than any individual is likely to have the time or energy to do on their own.

q.stem: What may result from increasing application of recommendation engines in our consumption of culture?

Consumers will actually enjoy better luck.
It will be easier to decide on what to enjoy.
Humans will develop tastes similar to machines'.

items.text:
America is stuck in a debate about teaching children to read that has been going on for decades. Some advocate teaching symbol-sound relationships (the sound k can be spelled as c, k, ck, or ch), known as phonics. Others support an immersive approach (using pictures of a cat to learn the word cat), known as “whole language . Most teachers today, almost three out of four according to a survey by the EdWeek Research Centre in 2019, use a mix called "balanced literacy". This combination of methods is ineffective. "You can't sprinkle in a little phonics, says Tenette Smith, executive director of elementary education and reading at Mississippi's education department. “It has to be systematic and explicitly taught."
Mississippi, often behind in social policy, has set an example here. In a state once notorious for its low reading scores, the Mississippi state legislature passed new literacy standards in 2013. Since then Mississippi has seen remarkable gains. Its fourth graders have moved from 49th (out of 50 states) to 29th on the National Assessment of Educational Progress, a nationwide exam. In 2019 it was the only state to improve its scores. For the first time since measurement began, Mississippi's pupils are now average readers, a remarkable achievement in such a poor state.

q.stem: What has America been witnessing for decades?
options: An obsession with innovating teaching methodologies of reading.
An enduring debate over the approach to teaching children to read.
An increasing concern with many children's inadequacy in literacy.
An ever-forceful advocacy of a combined method for teaching reading.
q.explain: 正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「America is stuck in a debate about teaching children to read that has been going on for decades.」

items.cn: 美国陷入了一场持续数十年的关于如何教孩子阅读的争论。一些人主张教授符号与声音的对应关系（音素启蒙法：k 的音可以拼写作 c、k、ck 或 ch），另一些人支持沉浸式方法（用猫的图片来学习 cat 这个词），即「整体语言法」。如今大多数教师——据教育周刊研究中心 2019 年的调查，约四分之三——使用一种称为「平衡读写法」的混合方式。这种方法的组合是无效的。「你不能只撒一点音素启蒙的佐料，」密西西比州教育部基础教育与阅读事务执行主任特妮特·史密斯说，「它必须系统性地、明确地教授。」在社会政策上常常落后的密西西比州，这次却树立了榜样。在这个曾因阅读成绩低下而臭名昭著的州，州议会在 2013 年通过了新的读写能力标准。从那以后，密西西比州取得了显著进步。该州四年级学生在全国教育进展评估（一项全国性考试）中的排名从第 49 名（共 50 个州）升至第 29 名。2019 年，它是唯一成绩提高的州。自开始测评以来，密西西比州的小学生首次达到了平均阅读水平——在这样一个贫困的州，这是了不起的成就。

items.text:
How on earth did we come to this? We protect our children obsessively from every harm; we scrutinize every carer, teacher or doctor with whom they come into contact. Yet despite all this, one group, which in no way has their best interests at heart, has almost unconstrained access.
We seem to take it for granted that advertisers and marketers are allowed to condition even the youngest children. Before children have even developed a proper sense of their own identity, or learned to handle money, they're encouraged to associate status and self-worth with stuff, and to look to external things such as fame and wealth for validation. We're turning out little consumers rather than young citizens who will value themselves for what they contribute to the society in which they live.

q.stem: Which group of people does the author say has almost unrestricted access to children?
options: Advertisers.
Carers.
Teachers.
Doctors.
q.explain: 正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Yet despite all this, one group, which in no way has their best interests at heart, has almost unconstrained access.」

It is rooted in our desire for material possessions.

items.text:
Psychologically speaking, competition has been seen as an inevitable consequence of human drives. According to Sigmund Freud, humans are born screaming for attention and full of organic drives for fulfillment in various areas. Initially, we compete for the attention of our parents. Thereafter, we are at the mercy of a battle between our base impulses for self-fulfillment and social and cultural norms which prohibit pure indulgence.
Current work in _anthropology_ (人类学) has suggested, however, that this view of the role of competition in human behavior may be incorrect. Thomas Hobbes, one of the great philosophers of the seventeenth century, is perhaps best remembered for his characterization of the “natural world,” that is, the world before the imposition of the will of humanity, as being “nasty, brutish, and short.” This image of the pre-rational world is still widely held, reinforced by Charles Darwin's highly influential work, _The Origin of Species_, which established the doctrine of natural selection. This doctrine, which takes for granted that those species best able to adapt to and master the natural environment in which they live will survive, has suggested that the struggle for survival is an inherent human trait which determines a person's success. Darwin's theory has even been summarized as “survival of the fittest” — a phrase Darwin himself never used — further highlighting competition's role in success.

q.stem: What does the author think is easy to see in many areas of contemporary life?
options: The disagreement on the inevitability of competition.
The consequence of psychological investigation.
The effect of human drives.
The impact of competition.
q.explain: 正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Psychologically speaking, competition has been seen as an inevitable consequence of human drives.」

items.cn: 从心理学角度看，竞争一直被视为人类驱力的必然结果。按照西格蒙德·弗洛伊德的说法，人类生下来就哭喊着索取关注，充满在各个方面寻求满足的有机驱力。最初，我们争夺父母的关注。此后，我们便受制于一场拉锯：一方是自我满足的原始冲动，另一方是禁止纯粹放纵的社会文化规范。然而，人类学的当前研究表明，这种关于竞争在人类行为中作用的观点可能并不正确。托马斯·霍布斯是十七世纪伟大的哲学家之一，最为人铭记的或许是他把「自然状态」——即人类意志强加于世界之前的状态——描绘成「肮脏、野蛮而短促」。这幅前理性世界的图景至今仍广为流传，并得到查尔斯·达尔文影响深远的著作《物种起源》的强化，该书确立了自然选择学说。这一学说理所当然地认为，最能适应并驾驭自身所处自然环境的物种才能生存下来，由此暗示生存斗争是一种决定个人成败的内在人类特质。达尔文的理论甚至被概括为「适者生存」——达尔文本人从未使用过这个短语——进一步凸显了竞争在成功中的作用。

items.text: Many studies have been conducted to test the importance placed on competition as opposed to other values, such as cooperation — by various cultures, and generally conclude that Americans uniquely praise competition as natural, inevitable, and desirable. In 1937, the world-renowned anthropologist Margaret Mead published _Cooperation and Competition among Primitive Peoples_, based on her studies of several societies that did not prize competition, and, in fact, seemed at times to place a negative value on it. One such society was the Zuni Indians of Arizona, and they, Mead found, valued cooperation far more than competition. After studying dozens of such cultures, Mead's final conclusion was that competitiveness is a culturally created aspect of human behavior, and that its prevalence in a particular society is relative to how that society values it.

q.stem: What conclusion did Margaret Mead reach after studying dozens of different cultures?
options: It is characteristic of humans to be competitive.
Americans are uniquely opposed to cooperation.
Competition is relatively more prevalent in Western societies.
People's attitude towards competition is actually culture-bound.
q.explain: 正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Many studies have been conducted to test the importance placed on competition as opposed to other values, such as cooperation — by various cultures, and generally conclude that Americans uniquely praise competition as natural, inevitable, and desirable.」

items.cn: 人们进行了许多研究，检验不同文化对竞争（相对于合作等其他价值观）的重视程度，结论大体一致：唯独美国人把竞争赞颂为自然的、不可避免的、可取的。1937 年，举世闻名的人类学家玛格丽特·米德出版了《原始民族的合作与竞争》，该书基于她对几个不崇尚竞争的社会的研究——这些社会有时甚至对竞争持负面评价。其中一个是亚利桑那州的祖尼印第安人，米德发现，他们对合作的重视远甚于竞争。在研究了数十个这样的文化之后，米德的最终结论是：竞争性是人类行为中由文化塑造的一面，它在特定社会中盛行的程度，取决于该社会对它的评价高低。

items.text:
Many researchers seem to be content with sharing the results of their studies in academic journals or at conferences. But few journals allow everybody to read the findings. Even articles freely available are usually written in academic language incomprehensible to the average reader.
For researchers in the tenure-track system, their main goal is winning tenure, which in part can be achieved by getting a number of papers published in prominent journals. Pressures like this mean community-level outreach is not prioritized.
Many researchers lack the writing skills to describe their results to a general audience. They may also worry about whether the public will understand their findings, or about findings being used to influence controversial policies. These concerns cause some researchers to shy away from communicating their findings outside the academic community.

q.stem: Why do ordinary readers find it difficult to access the results of researchers' studies?
options: They cannot understand the academic language used for reporting these results.
They feel intimidated by the jargon researchers use to describe their findings.
They do not attend conferences where these results are freely available.
They have few chances to locate the journals that publish these findings.
q.explain: 正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「For researchers in the tenure-track system, their main goal is winning tenure, which in part can be achieved by getting a number of papers published in prominent journals.」

items.cn: 许多研究者似乎满足于在学术期刊或学术会议上分享研究成果。但很少有期刊允许所有人阅读这些发现。即使是免费获取的文章，通常也用普通读者难以理解的学术语言写成。对于终身教职体系中的研究者来说，他们的主要目标是赢得终身教职，而这在一定程度上可以通过在知名期刊上发表论文来实现。诸如此类的压力意味着面向社区的科普传播不会被优先考虑。许多研究者缺乏向普通读者描述其成果的写作技巧。他们也可能担心公众能否理解他们的发现，或者担心研究成果被用来影响有争议的政策。这些顾虑使一些研究者回避在学术界之外传播自己的发现。

items.text:
The benefits of sharing findings flow both ways. Engaging with other researchers and the public can lead to unexpected new connections and new ideas that could suggest fruitful new directions for research.
To benefit both researchers and the communities, the need to find innovative, accessible ways to share the work cannot be overstated.
Institutions and funding organizations should support more researchers to publish in open access journals so that the public doesn't have to pay to read them. Institutions and researchers should invest in partnerships that expand capacity for sharing results more broadly.
Furthermore, ethics committees should make it mandatory for researchers to share their results with the public. Every research participant should opt in or out of receiving results, as part of the process of giving informed consent.

q.stem: How can sharing findings benefit researchers themselves?
options: By helping them to identify new research directions.
By enabling them to understand crises plaguing society.
By enabling them to effectively address social discrepancies.
By helping them to forge ties with government agencies.
q.explain: 正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Institutions and researchers should invest in partnerships that expand capacity for sharing results more broadly.」

items.cn: 分享研究成果的好处是双向的。与其他研究者和公众交流，可以带来意想不到的新联系和新想法，为研究提示富有成果的新方向。为了让研究者和社区双双受益，寻找创新的、通俗易懂的成果分享方式，其重要性怎么强调都不为过。机构和资助组织应当支持更多研究者在开放获取期刊上发表论文，让公众不必付费阅读。机构和研究者应当投入建设伙伴关系，扩展更广泛分享成果的能力。此外，伦理委员会应强制要求研究者向公众分享其成果。每一位研究参与者都应在知情同意的过程中选择是否接收研究结果。

Does this perhaps explain, in part, the lack of data about how spiders are faring in our age of ecological crisis? British butterflies are the most studied group of insects in the world, due to the long tradition of collecting and observing them. But spider conservationists point out that it was only in the 1980s that the classification of house spiders was properly sorted out. And while information about insect populations is gathered by experiments that measure the numbers hitting windscreens or traps, there have been few attempts to count spiders.
The huge reductions in the numbers of flying insects can only mean a reduction in spiders' food supply. A recent landmark study identified a 75% fall in insect populations between 1989 and 2016, with pesticide use thought to be to blame along with the destruction of wild areas for development. This means the overall picture for spiders is worrying, as it is for most creatures. But conservationists are most concerned about those varieties that are threatened due to habitat loss and fragmentation, which makes it impossible for them to migrate.

q.stem: What partly accounts for the reduction in spiders' food supply?
options: The long tradition of collecting insects.
Fast reproduction of their competitors.
Chemicals used for killing insects.
The extinction of a lot of wildlife.
q.explain: 正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「Does this perhaps explain, in part, the lack of data about how spiders are faring in our age of ecological crisis?」

items.cn: 这能否部分解释，在我们这个生态危机时代，关于蜘蛛处境的数据为何如此匮乏？由于长期采集和观察的传统，英国蝴蝶是世界上被研究得最多的昆虫类群。但蜘蛛保护人士指出，直到 20 世纪 80 年代，家蜘蛛的分类才得到 properly（妥善）梳理。虽然昆虫种群的信息是通过统计撞上车挡风玻璃或落入陷阱的数量等实验收集的，却几乎没有人尝试去数过蜘蛛。飞虫数量的大幅减少只能意味着蜘蛛的食物供应在减少。最近一项里程碑式的研究发现，1989 年至 2016 年间昆虫种群减少了 75%，人们认为罪魁祸首是杀虫剂的使用以及荒野因开发而遭到破坏。这意味着蜘蛛的总体前景令人担忧，大多数生物亦然。但保护人士最担心的是那些因栖息地丧失和碎片化而受威胁、无法迁徙的品种。

The huge reductions in the numbers of flying insects can only mean a reduction in spiders' food supply. A recent landmark study identified a 75% fall in insect populations between 1989 and 2016, with pesticide use thought to be to blame along with the destruction of wild areas for development. This means the overall picture for spiders is worrying, as it is for most creatures. But conservationists are most concerned about those varieties that are threatened due to habitat loss and fragmentation, which makes it impossible for them to migrate.
Of around 650 spider species regularly recorded in the UK, the majority thrive in marshes and wasteland. Conservation efforts, often led by determined individuals, have helped some species to recover by reintroducing them to new areas. With rewilding now firmly on the environmental policy agenda, the hope is that in future, spiders will be enabled to migrate by themselves, adapting to climate change by moving along wildlife corridors.

q.stem: What does the passage say is conservationists' biggest worry?
options: A variety of spiders are threatened due to pollution of marshes and wasteland.
Certain species of spiders are endangered due to loss of their natural homes.
An increasing number of spiders are being killed by deadly pesticides.
More and more spider species are found losing their ability to migrate.
q.explain: 正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「But conservationists are most concerned about those varieties that are threatened due to habitat loss and fragmentation, which makes it impossible for them to migrate.」

q.stem: What wish does the author express close to the end of the passage?
